pre_context.text: I do not know how to tell my husband that I am lonely and I want out of the marriage

reference_transcript.text: Hi
Hello! How are you today?
Ok I guess
I do not know how to tell my husband that I am lonely and I want out of the marriage
Oh, that sure is a heavy subject and a heavy thing to be on your mind.
He is not one you can talk to he usually just brushes things off
So you have tried to discuss your loneliness with your husband before?
Yes he tells me it’s just in my head and I could just go out with him, but he drinks then to much so I do not like going out with him
I am sure that is frustrating! Does he drink at home as well or just when you go out?
Just when he goes out I do not go with him I do not drink and drive
And he hangs with some obnoxious people
Would a date night at home with take-out and a movie just the two of you be an option?
He would go to sleep , and then he thinks I am crazy he says we are no kids anymore that need to go on a date we are married
Do you think you both might be open to talking to a marriage counselor?
I want that but I doubt he will talk he tells me he has no problems I have them, and all it does is I doubt myself
I turned this situation in every direction and I just am not able to find a solution
Well, what about you finding a counselor for yourself who could help you with your own self-care? Perhaps it could be a start and then he/she could help you end your marriage if you still want to.
It took me awhile to learn my own value and how important self-care is.
You know what I like that idea
Maybe you are right  I might get then some self esteem as well again
I know from experience that our self esteem suffers when we're in an unhappy marriage. It takes a lot of courage to seek help so I applaud you!
Thank you you are very kind
I'm glad I could help and I wish you the best of luck!
I always think when he acts these ways it’s me because I am not pretty enough or have few pounds to muc
Thank stay safe

cognitive_style: I am in a low, heavy mood that makes hopeful claims feel unreal — I come to believe change only gradually, when it shows up in small felt steps, not when someone asserts it. I need gentle, patient listening before I can put my feelings into words; pressure or quick fixes make me withdraw. I hesitate to act on what I want until someone shows me a small, safe step. Small signs of being truly understood lift me noticeably.
